audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls Fiora "he/his" throughout, and Level 3, First item and 2+ items are marked Fiora while carrying Akshan-favoured boilerplate whys.
audit.why: Fiora is female. The lane genuinely flips at 3 when Riposte and Lunge are both up, and again at Tiamat — the content layer already says so, but the full layer's stage text never matched its own side fields.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed and the three contradicted stages now state the Fiora-side reason: Riposte plus Lunge at 3, the Tiamat shove at first item, and an itemised Fiora out-duelling and out-splitting you at two.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike said "her R is just a Fiora dash", and repeated it in whys[4].
audit.why: Grand Challenge (R, 110/90/70) is not a dash. Riot's description: it reveals all four Vitals on a target, grants Fiora move speed near them, and heals her and nearby allies if she hits all four or the target dies. Calling it a dash tells you to respect a gap-close that does not exist while ignoring the heal that actually decides the extended fight.
audit.corrected: Both strings now describe Grand Challenge as a four-Vital reveal that heals her, and Riposte's 24s rank-1 cooldown is stated as the real level-6 gate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Riposte is described in six strings across both layers as parrying and then STUNNING you — "if she parries the cast she stuns you out of it", "negates the damage and stuns you", "you eat a stun", "gets parried and stunned", plus the full layer's cooldown line and interactions report.
audit.why: Riot's description is explicit: Riposte's stab "slows the first enemy champion hit, OR stuns them if Fiora blocked an immobilizing effect with this ability". Akshan's kit contains no immobilizing effect — Dirty Fighting, Avengerang, Going Rogue, Heroic Swing and Comeuppance carry no stun, root, knockup or grounding. Against Akshan specifically, Riposte can only ever slow. Six strings told the reader to fear a stun that cannot happen, which changes whether you commit at all.
audit.corrected: Every instance now says Riposte blanks the damage and slows, and states plainly that it cannot stun you because you bring no CC for it to block. Riposte's real 24/22/20/18/16s cooldown is now given as the window to trade in.

edits.before: Level 1 is a wash — you have one passive second shot and Avengerang (Q), she has one ability, so just last-hit. Your one real window is 2-3: the second passive shot plus Q chip her if you fire from max range, where her Q-dash and Riposte can't reach, and you never walk into vital range. The trap is Riposte (W) — it parries a targeted ability or key cast, so if you throw Q or auto into a ready parry she negates the damage and stuns you. Trade only once you've seen her W go on cooldown or baited it out, and remember your Heroic Swing (E) needs nearby terrain to escape, so don't poke from spots where you can't swing away.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash — you have one passive second shot and Avengerang (Q), she has one ability, so just last-hit. Your one real window is 2-3: the second passive shot plus Q chip her if you fire from max range, where her Lunge and Riposte can't reach, and you never walk into Vital range. The trap is Riposte (W) — 24s at rank 1, it parries all incoming damage for a beat and then slows you; it only stuns if it blocks CC, and you bring none. Trade once you've seen her W spent or baited, and remember your Heroic Swing (E) needs nearby terrain to escape, so don't poke from spots where you can't swing away.

edits.before: This is where the lane slips. Heroic Swing (E) is your poke AND your escape, but it only hooks into terrain — on an open stretch of lane it's a stranded long cast she can read. If she Q-dashes onto a vital as you swing, or saves Riposte for the exact cast, you eat a stun and her passive starts ticking percent-max-HP true damage off your tiny pool. Pre-place E on a wall before you commit and never swing into her when her parry is up. At 6 your R (Comeuppance) is a lock-on pick tool, not a duel button — she can Riposte the channel and stun you, and her own R is just a dash, so don't count on bursting her down face to face. Use camo W to roam and cash your range elsewhere instead of forcing a fight you lose.

edits.before: You lose the straight 1v1 outright once she has items — her passive vital true damage scales with her bruiser build and ignores your shieldless lethality, and she out-splits you with better dueling and waveclear. Worse, she can Riposte the single key cast your kill relies on (your E swing or your R), so even a perfect setup gets parried and stunned. Your only path is to have already snowballed off your level 2-5 poke window or off camo-W roams, then group and use R as a long-range pick from safety. Never sidelane into a fed Fiora; let your team answer her splitpush while you take other map plays.

Your only path is to have already snowballed off your level 2-5 poke window or off camo-W roams, then group and use R as a long-range pick from safety. Never sidelane into a fed Fiora; let your team answer her splitpush while you take other map plays.

notes: The page repeatedly calls Fiora's Vital damage 'percent-max-HP true damage'. Riot's Duelist's Dance description only says hitting a Vital restores Health and grants Move Speed — no damage type at all — and the kit file flags the passive as heal-only while flagging trueDamage on Grand Challenge. I could not verify the true-damage claim from the kit, so per the rules those strings were left untouched and logged as unverified. Same for the kit's revealsStealth flag on Grand Challenge: Riot's text says it reveals Vitals, not stealth, so nothing was written about it revealing Going Rogue camouflage. That one matters and is worth someone confirming.
